pages.summary: NetCDF files: variables made, written and read.
body: NetCDF holds arrays with named dimensions and attributes, the usual format of climate and ocean data. `nccreate` makes a variable (and the file and dimensions when they are not there yet; a length of Inf makes a dimension unlimited), with a data type, format, fill value and compression. `ncwrite` writes values, from a start and with a stride if given; `ncread` reads a variable, or a part of it by start, count and stride. Sizes are in the language's order (the first dimension varying fastest), the reverse of the file's; `scale_factor`, `add_offset` and `_FillValue` are applied on reading and writing.
syntax: With its type, format, fill value and compression.
vardata = ncread(source, varname, start, count, stride)

pages.summary: What a NetCDF file holds, printed or as a struct; and its attributes read and written.
body: `ncinfo` gives the file's dimensions, variables, attributes, groups and format (or a variable's), `ncdisp` prints them. Attributes belong to a variable, or to the file itself (location `'/'`): units, long names, history.

pages.summary: Tables as Parquet files, and back.
body: Parquet stores a table by columns, compressed, keeping each column's type: the usual format for large data sets passed between programs. Numbers keep their class, text becomes strings, times datetimes and durations, categories categorical. `parquetread` can read some variables only, or give a timetable; `parquetinfo` describes the file.

pages.summary: FITS files, the astronomers' format for images and tables: written, read and described.
body: `fitswrite` writes an array as an image (its class kept; `'append'` adds an image extension). `fitsread` reads the primary image, or an extension, table, region or raw values; images are scaled by `BSCALE` and `BZERO` to double. `fitsinfo` lists the parts and their header keywords, and `fitsdisp` prints the headers.
